catalog_quote: The stress will fall on the ultimate syllable or on the penultimate syllable, which means that it will fall on one of the last two syllables at the right edge of the lexical word, as shown in the examples. ... Stress is not sensitive to syllable weight. (2.92) (a) /takɨɾap/ [dɔˈkɨɾap̚] 'spider-monkey' (b) /tojtõna/ [tojˈtõna] 'boss' (c) /kapkaba/ [kɔp̚ˈgaba] 'flute (four holes)' (d) /tawtʃe/ [tawˈtʃɛ] 'peccary' ... The stress will fall on the ultimate or on the penultimate syllable (unpredictable), which means that it will fall on one of the last two syllables at the right edge of the lexical word. ... In TRISYLLABIC and other POLYSYLLABIC forms (words of more than three syllables), the stress may fall either on the second or on the first right-most edge of the word. DISYLLABIC words have either ultimate or penultimate stress. The stress pattern of disyllabic words may suggest possible …

audit.reasoning: Quote verified verbatim at the stated pages in the held 2014 dissertation, which is the fullest and only substantial description of Akuntsú prosody (reference grammar with acoustic measurements, by the sole fieldworker). The earlier 2008 MA thesis (fetched sources to gives the same final/penult window and defers analysis to future work. Coding 'lexical, right-edge two-syllable window, weight-insensitive' matches the author's explicit statements; the only caveat worth carrying in a caution field is that the author herself calls the analysis tentative and elsewhere (§2.4.5 p.105, §2.6 p.117) characterises the language as iambic with final stress as the majority pattern and no 4+-syllable word attested with final stress — a 'final-default with lexical penult' reading is possible but the source's own word is 'unpredictable', so no recode is warrant

sources.quote: 'O acento na língua Akuntsú pode ocorrer na última e na penúltima sílaba' (p. 78, with lists of final-stressed e.g. [kiˈdap̚] 'cera', [kiɾiˈto] 'aranha' and penult-stressed e.g. [kɔp̚ˈgaba] 'flauta', [ˈpɛbo] 'pena', [ˈtʃami] 'bom'); 'Esperamos descrever a situação fonológica do acento em estudos futuros' (p. 79); summary p. 81: 'pode ocorrer na última e na penúltima sílaba, aparentemente sem caráter distintivo.'
